fit: acute lemon balm extract capsules and subjective mood factors in healthy adults
assessment: In 20 healthy volunteers, Figure 3 shows a smaller calmness decline with 300 mg than placebo at 1 and 2.5 hours and with 900 mg at 1 hour. Alertness was lower after 900 mg at all measured times; contentedness was unchanged on the reported comparison. The acute mood scales did not measure clinical depression, and neither Parkinson disease nor brewed lemon balm was tested.

fit: concentrated aqueous extract beverage and acute anxiety in healthy adults
assessment: The fruit-sweetened lower-dose drink favored state anxiety against an artificially sweetened placebo, and the high-dose drink with the same artificial sweeteners as placebo favored worse anxiety at a disputed timepoint. Yoghurt fatigue varied by hour. The source tests industrial extract and acute outcomes outside Parkinson disease, with no clinical depression measure. The retrospective registry differs in doses and includes an unreported bar arm.
